correctness.rationale: At positive x, mass integration of (1-u)u’=-chi u gives M=(m/chi)(u0-u0²/2), u0=1-sqrt(delta). The normalized U=u(|X|) density is m(1-u)/(M chi). W=chi/(1-U), Jacobian du/dw=chi/w² gives exactly m chi/(M w³) on (chi,chi/sqrt(delta)); q=2 integration gives I_delta=m chi log(1/delta)/(2M). At delta=0 u=1-sqrt(2chi_c|x|)+O(|x|); sqrt(p)=sqrt(chi_c)-(chi_c/sqrt2)sqrt(|x|)+O(|x|). Both sides of square-root cusp produce ∫(Δsqrt p)²~(chi_c²/4)h² log(1/|h|), so H²~chi_c² h² log(1/(chi_c|h|))/8 under the given half-integral convention. For fixed delta>0 sqrt(p) in H¹ gives H²=I h²/8+o(h²). Finite-return statement applies to total normalized stationary density only; source local flux equations supply the model premise.
